ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $E$ is a moving point on the side $CD$ of square $ABCD$, with $AB=2$. Connect $BE$, and draw $AF \perp BE$, which intersects $BC$ at $F$ and $BE$ at $G$. Connect $CG$. When $CG$ is at its minimum value, what is the length of $CF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in Figure 1, take the midpoint O of AB, and connect OG and OC.\\
$\because$ Quadrilateral ABCD is a square,\\
$\therefore \angle ABC=90^\circ$,\\
$\because$AB=2,\\
$\therefore$OB=OA=1,\\
$\therefore$OC=$\sqrt{1^2+2^2}=\sqrt{5}$,\\
$\because$AF$\perp$BE,\\
$\therefore \angle AGB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ point G lies on the circle $\odot$O with AB as the diameter,\\
$\because$AO=OB,\\
$\therefore$OG=$\frac{1}{2}$AB=1,\\
$\therefore$ when O, G, and C are collinear, the value of CG is minimum, and the minimum value=$\sqrt{5}-1$ (as shown in Figure 2),\\
$\because$OB=OG=1,\\
$\therefore \angle OBG=\angle OGB$,\\
$\because$AB$\parallel$CD,\\
$\therefore \angle OBG=\angle CEG$,\\
$\because \angle OGB=\angle CGE$,\\
$\therefore \angle CGE=\angle CEG$,\\
$\therefore$CE=CG=$\sqrt{5}-1$,\\
$\because \angle ABF=\angle BCE=\angle AGB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BAF+\angle ABG=90^\circ$, $\angle ABG+\angle CBE=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BAF=\angle CBE$,\\
$\because$AB=BC,\\
$\therefore \triangle ABF \cong \triangle BCE$ (ASA),\\
$\therefore$BF=CE=$\sqrt{5}-1$,\\
$\therefore$CF=BC−BF=2−($\sqrt{5}-1$)=3−$\sqrt{5}$,\\
Therefore, $CF = \boxed{3-\sqrt{5}}$

method.method_draft: Synthetic locus method. First read the diagram as a square ABCD with A upper-left, B lower-left, C lower-right, D upper-right; E lies on side CD, BE is drawn, AF is perpendicular to BE and meets BC at F and BE at G, and CG is drawn. From the text use AB=2 and E moving on CD. Let O be the midpoint of AB. Since ∠AGB=90° because AF ⟂ BE and G lies on both lines, G lies on the circle with diameter AB, centered at O with radius 1. The fixed point C has OC=sqrt(OB^2+BC^2)=sqrt(1^2+2^2)=sqrt5, so CG is minimized when C, G, O are collinear, giving CG_min=sqrt5-1. In that minimum position, use OB=OG and AB ∥ CD to derive angle equalities showing triangle CEG is isosceles, so CE=CG=sqrt5-1. Finally compare right triangles ABF and BCE: ∠ABF=∠BCE=90°, AB=BC=2, and the acute angles match because AF ⟂ BE and BC ⟂ CD; hence the triangles are congruent and BF=CE=sqrt5-1. Therefore CF=BC-BF=2-(sqrt5-1)=3-sqrt5.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中是一个正方形 ABCD，A 在左上，B 在左下，C 在右下，D 在右上；E 位于右侧边 CD 上；从 B 连到 E；从 A 向下作一条线与 BE 垂直，交 BC 于 F，交 BE 于 G；图中还连接了 C 和 G。推理：取 AB 的中点 O。因为 ABCD 是正方形且 AB=2，所以 OA=OB=1，BC=2，且 OC=sqrt(1^2+2^2)=sqrt5。由于 AF ⟂ BE，且 G 同时在 AF 和 BE 上，所以 ∠AGB=90°，因此 G 在以 AB 为直径、O 为圆心、半径 1 的圆上。对于固定点 C，CG 的最小值出现在 O、G、C 共线且 G 在 OC 上时，所以 CG_min=OC-OG=sqrt5-1。此时 OB=OG=1，所以 ∠OBG=∠OGB。又 AB ∥ CD，且 E 在 CD 上，所以 ∠OBG=∠CEG；O、G、C 共线，所以 ∠OGB=∠CGE。于是 ∠CEG=∠CGE，三角形 CEG 等腰，CE=CG=sqrt5-1。再比较三角形 ABF 和 BCE：∠ABF=∠BCE=90°，AB=BC=2；又 AF ⟂ BE，BC ⟂ CD，可得 ∠BAF=∠CBE，因此 △ABF ≅ △BCE，得到 BF=CE=sqrt5-1。于是 CF=BC-BF=2-(sqrt5-1)=3-sqrt5。

solver_metadata.cot_raw: 图像描述：图中是一个正方形 ABCD，A 在左上，B 在左下，C 在右下，D 在右上；E 位于右侧边 CD 上；从 B 连到 E；从 A 向下作一条线与 BE 垂直，交 BC 于 F，交 BE 于 G；图中还连接了 C 和 G。推理：取 AB 的中点 O。因为 ABCD 是正方形且 AB=2，所以 OA=OB=1，BC=2，且 OC=sqrt(1^2+2^2)=sqrt5。由于 AF ⟂ BE，且 G 同时在 AF 和 BE 上，所以 ∠AGB=90°，因此 G 在以 AB 为直径、O 为圆心、半径 1 的圆上。对于固定点 C，CG 的最小值出现在 O、G、C 共线且 G 在 OC 上时，所以 CG_min=OC-OG=sqrt5-1。此时 OB=OG=1，所以 ∠OBG=∠OGB。又 AB ∥ CD，且 E 在 CD 上，所以 ∠OBG=∠CEG；O、G、C 共线，所以 ∠OGB=∠CGE。于是 ∠CEG=∠CGE，三角形 CEG 等腰，CE=CG=sqrt5-1。再比较三角形 ABF 和 BCE：∠ABF=∠BCE=90°，AB=BC=2；又 AF ⟂ BE，BC ⟂ CD，可得 ∠BAF=∠CBE，因此 △ABF ≅ △BCE，得到 BF=CE=sqrt5-1。于是 CF=BC-BF=2-(sqrt5-1)=3-sqrt5。

method.method_draft: Coordinate optimization method. Read the diagram as a square with B at the lower-left, C lower-right, A upper-left, D upper-right, E on the right side CD, F on the bottom side BC, and G the intersection of AF and BE. Set coordinates B=(0,0), C=(2,0), A=(0,2), D=(2,2). Let E=(2,t), where 0≤t≤2. Then BE has slope t/2. Since AF ⟂ BE and passes through A, AF has slope -2/t and equation y=2-(2/t)x, so its intersection with BC, where y=0, is F=(t,0). Thus CF=2-t, so it remains to find t when CG is minimized. Find G by intersecting BE: y=(t/2)x with AF: y=2-(2/t)x, giving G=(4t/(t^2+4), 2t^2/(t^2+4)). Then write CG^2=(2-4t/(t^2+4))^2+(2t^2/(t^2+4))^2. Differentiate this expression on 0≤t≤2; after simplification the critical condition is t^2+2t-4=0, so t=sqrt5-1. Check endpoints or monotonicity sign to confirm this is the minimum. Therefore CF=2-t=2-(sqrt5-1)=3-sqrt5.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, $E$ is a moving point on the side $CD$ of square $ABCD$, with $AB=2$. Connect $BE$, and draw $AF \perp BE$, which intersects $BC$ at $F$ and $BE$ at $G$. Connect $CG$. When $CG$ is at its minimum value, what is the length of $CF$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in Figure 1, take the midpoint O of AB, and connect OG and OC.\\
$\because$ Quadrilateral ABCD is a square,\\
$\therefore \angle ABC=90^\circ$,\\
$\because$AB=2,\\
$\therefore$OB=OA=1,\\
$\therefore$OC=$\sqrt{1^2+2^2}=\sqrt{5}$,\\
$\because$AF$\perp$BE,\\
$\therefore \angle AGB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ point G lies on the circle $\odot$O with AB as the diameter,\\
$\because$AO=OB,\\
$\therefore$OG=$\frac{1}{2}$AB=1,\\
$\therefore$ when O, G, and C are collinear, the value of CG is minimum, and the minimum value=$\sqrt{5}-1$ (as shown in Figure 2),\\
$\because$OB=OG=1,\\
$\therefore \angle OBG=\angle OGB$,\\
$\because$AB$\parallel$CD,\\
$\therefore \angle OBG=\angle CEG$,\\
$\because \angle OGB=\angle CGE$,\\
$\therefore \angle CGE=\angle CEG$,\\
$\therefore$CE=CG=$\sqrt{5}-1$,\\
$\because \angle ABF=\angle BCE=\angle AGB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BAF+\angle ABG=90^\circ$, $\angle ABG+\angle CBE=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BAF=\angle CBE$,\\
$\because$AB=BC,\\
$\therefore \triangle ABF \cong \triangle BCE$ (ASA),\\
$\therefore$BF=CE=$\sqrt{5}-1$,\\
$\therefore$CF=BC−BF=2−($\sqrt{5}-1$)=3−$\sqrt{5}$,\\
Therefore, $CF = \boxed{3-\sqrt{5}}$
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a square ABCD, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, D is at the upper right; E is located on the right side CD; connect from B to E; draw a line downward from A perpendicular to BE, intersecting BC at F and BE at G; the figure also connects C and G. Reasoning: Take the midpoint O of AB. Because ABCD is a square and AB=2, OA=OB=1, BC=2, and OC=sqrt(1^2+2^2)=sqrt5. Since AF ⟂ BE, and G is simultaneously on AF and BE, ∠AGB=90°, therefore G is on the circle with AB as diameter, O as center, and radius 1. For the fixed point C, the minimum value of CG occurs when O, G, C are collinear and G is on OC, so CG_min=OC-OG=sqrt5-1. At this time OB=OG=1, so ∠OBG=∠OGB. Also AB ∥ CD, and E is on CD, so ∠OBG=∠CEG; O, G, C are collinear, so ∠OGB=∠CGE. Thus ∠CEG=∠CGE, triangle CEG is isosceles, CE=CG=sqrt5-1. Then compare triangles ABF and BCE: ∠ABF=∠BCE=90°, AB=BC=2; also AF ⟂ BE, BC ⟂ CD, so ∠BAF=∠CBE, therefore △ABF ≅ △BCE, obtaining BF=CE=sqrt5-1. Thus CF=BC-BF=2-(sqrt5-1)=3-sqrt5.
